command: fabio data-agent query --workspace $WS_ID --id $AGENT_ID --prompt "What are the top 5 products by revenue?"
description: Queries a published Data Agent with a natural language question over the OpenAI-compatible Assistants endpoint. Returns the agent's answer and the threadId used for the run (reuse it for a multi-turn follow-up). Only a published agent is queryable; the draft/staging stage has no public endpoint.

data.question: What are the top 5 products by revenue?
data.answer: The top 5 products by revenue are: Widget Pro ($1.2M), Gadget X ($980K), SuperTool ($875K), MegaPack ($720K), BasicKit ($650K).

notes: Only --stage production (published, the default) is supported — querying a draft/sandbox agent is not available via the public Fabric API (publish first with `fabio data-agent publish`). The published consumption URL is auto-constructed; pass --published-url only to target a specific endpoint. MULTI-TURN: pass --keep-thread to retain the thread, then reuse its threadId on the next call with --thread-id to continue the conversation. FILES: pass --download-files <dir> to save any files the answer attaches (generated CSVs/charts) into <dir>; the response then includes a `files` array. VISUALS: pass --visuals to extract chart specifications the agent generated — when it charts an answer it invokes a VisualizeDataset tool whose arguments carry the full spec (chart_type, x_column, y_columns, title, axis titles, sort, and the aggregated data as inline_csv_data); the response then includes a `visuals` array so a client can render the chart without the portal. (The pre-rendered report_specs_*.json file is NOT downloadable — its file id 404s on the published /files endpoint — but its content is redundant with the extracted spec.) Add --show-steps to include the SQL/tool-call run steps. Use --timeout to control max wait (default: 300s; Spark cold start can take minutes).

query_examples.description: Thread id to reuse for a multi-turn follow-up (--thread-id).
Local paths of any downloaded answer files (with --download-files).
Chart type of the first extracted visual (with --visuals), e.g. column_chart.
The aggregated data behind each chart (with --visuals).
